Container.Name: nexfolk
Container.Overview: Contacts for families and small groups on your own server. One container, SQLite, and a calm look of its own. Several address books per person, each shared with other accounts to read or to change, with a default book for new contacts. Favourites, labels and gift ideas stay yours alone, also in shared books; relations, anniversaries and a birthday without a year are kept beside the card. Contacts move in once from iCloud, Google or another CardDAV server, or are read along with changes written back, and vCard files go in and out at any time. Birthdays and anniversaries show on one page, with a reminder by mail or in the browser and as a calendar subscription; duplicates are found and merged, and address labels come out as PDF. A CardDAV server under /dav/ brings the address books to iPhone and iPad, Android with DAVx5, Thunderbird and Outlook, with a password per device and a QR code for the iPhone (needs https). nextime, nexmail, nexdiary, nextasks and nexpaper connect with one click. nexfolk installs from the browser as an app, speaks English and German, and has a REST API and an MCP server. Accounts come by invitation, with a second factor (TOTP), passkeys and sign-in through OpenID Connect providers. Backups run on a schedule and can be downloaded and restored. This is an early release: keep a backup and open an issue when something is wrong.
Container.Description: Contacts for families and small groups on your own server: several address books per person, shared to read or to change, birthdays in view, and a CardDAV server for iPhone and Android. Open the WebUI and create the first account; it becomes the operator. It needs the setup code from the container log (click the nexfolk icon, then Logs), a new one at every start until nexfolk is set up. To choose the code yourself, set Setup Code below. Further accounts come by invitation. Phones and other address book programs connect only over https: put nexfolk behind a reverse proxy with TLS, then set Public URL and Trusted Proxies. To have iOS show the iPhone profile as verified, map the folder with your web server's certificate under Certificates and name the two files in Profile Certificate and Profile Key. All data lives under /data: the SQLite database, contact photos, secret.key, backups, logs and your own languages. Keep it on a local disk, never on an SMB or NFS share, because SQLite locking is not reliable over network filesystems. Set PUID and PGID to the user that should own the files. 99 and 100 are the Unraid defaults and work out of the box.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port you reach nexfolk at. Container port: 8000

Config.Name: Data (Container Path: /data)
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database, contact photos, the key secret.key, backups, logs and your own languages. Keep it on a local disk, not on a network share.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that should own the files in /data. 99 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that should own the files in /data. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Time Zone
Config.Description: The server's time zone, for example Europe/Berlin: backups and birthday reminders run in it. Leave blank for UTC.

Config.Name: Setup Code
Config.Description: The code the first account needs to become the operator, at least 16 characters. Leave blank: nexfolk makes a new one at every start until it is set up and writes it to the container log.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The address people use to reach nexfolk, for example https://contacts.example.com when it sits behind a reverse proxy. Used for invitation links, the phone setup and the return address of OpenID Connect and Google. Leave blank to take the address of the request; the setting in the interface wins when set.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxies
Config.Description: Addresses or networks of your reverse proxies, comma separated, for example 172.16.0.0/12. Only their X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto are believed, so only they can tell nexfolk that a request came in over https (phones need that); without it every sign-in seems to come from the proxy and the brake against password guessing cannot tell people apart.

Config.Name: Container Port (host networking only)
Config.Description: Leave this empty unless you switched Network Type to Host. In bridge mode the WebUI Port above already does the job and setting this will break it, because the mapping still points at 8000. On host networking the port inside the container is the port on your server, so use this to move nexfolk off 8000 if something else is already there.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Protects the server-side secrets (the passwords of iCloud and other CardDAV accounts read along, the Google sign-ins, the client secrets of sign-in providers, the mail password, the seeds of second factors). Leave blank: nexfolk creates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key.

Config.Name: Certificates (Container Path: /certs)
Config.Description: Optional: a folder with your web server's certificate and key, for example the one of your reverse proxy with Let's Encrypt's fullchain.pem and privkey.pem. Only read, to sign the profile for iPhone and iPad.

Config.Name: Profile Certificate
Config.Description: The certificate with its chain the iPhone profile is signed with, for example /certs/fullchain.pem. Read anew for every profile, so a renewed certificate counts at once. Leave both this and Profile Key blank to hand out the profile unsigned (iOS then calls it not verified).

Config.Name: Profile Key
Config.Description: The private key belonging to Profile Certificate, for example /certs/privkey.pem.
